{"class": "one_plus_related",
 "explanation": "The unit responds to vertical objects with a narrow neck or waist that widens into a rounded or flared body, as with bottles, flasks, jugs, vases and bells. It responds more weakly to other objects with the same outline, such as flared skirts, gourds and coral-like shapes.",
 "evidence": "Most top activations are bottles, flasks, glassware, an amphora, a milk can, a bell and a coffee pot (10 down to 7), all with that narrow-to-wide shape. The lower-ranked dresses/skirts (#4, #13, #14), squash (#18) and cucumbers (#16) share the shape but are not containers.",
 "missing_data": "Activations on silhouettes or line drawings with the same shape, compared with containers lacking that shape (boxes, cans), would separate shape-tuning from bottle/container identity. A wider range of activation levels would show whether the dresses are true matches.",
 "confidence": 0.6}
